s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of abdominal pain, nausea, and bloody diarrhea with evidence of colonic inflammation
salient_findings: Colonoscopic findings of segmental erythema and ulceration
key_facts: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays
Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT
No evidence of perforation, abscess, or diverticulosis
Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy
Subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Segmental erythema and ulceration on colonoscopy, subepithelial edema and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy

shortlist.label: Crohn's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild thickening of the mid- and distal descending colon on CT, elevated C-reactive protein

shortlist.label: Infectious Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bloody diarrhea and evidence of colonic inflammation, despite negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays

shortlist.label: Microscopic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated fecal calprotectin and normal-appearing mucosa in some colon segments

shortlist.label: Ischemic Colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea, with evidence of colonic inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of segmental erythema and ulceration in the descending and sigmoid colon, with normal-appearing mucosa in other areas, along with subepithelial edema, hemorrhage, and acute inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy, is more consistent with Crohn's Disease, which can cause skip lesions and segmental inflammation.

rejected.label: Ulcerative Colitis
rejected.why: Typically involves the rectum and extends proximally in a continuous manner, which is not seen in this patient

rejected.label: Infectious Colitis
rejected.why: Negative stool cultures and Clostridioides difficile toxin assays make this less likely

rejected.label: Microscopic Colitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with chronic watery diarrhea and normal endoscopic appearance, which does not match this patient's symptoms and colonoscopy findings

rejected.label: Ischemic Colitis
rejected.why: Usually occurs in older patients and is associated with risk factors such as low blood flow or vasculopathy, which are not present in this patient
